body:
v4.0 Breaking (owner: the decimal defaults deferred to v4.0 are now due).
1. Remove the 3.x bounded Decimal and i128 numeric types. The exact tower becomes the only numeric API.
2. The default DivisionPolicy is EXACT when the quotient terminates (the reduced divisor has only the factors 2 and 5). Otherwise it keeps 18 fractional digits, rounded HALF-TO-EVEN. This replaces 3.x's default of 18 digits truncated. `exact`, `N` and `N:ROUNDING` stay available.
3. Temporal seconds are fully exact.

Cover the CLI, Rust, Python, C and wasm, the governor profile (a version bump with regenerated vectors), the CHANGELOG Breaking section and the book (with zh-Hans). Work in progress: branch `paudley/423-v4-decimal-defaults`. Refs #423.

git switch -c restore b0ed2f8c519f
base64 -d parts.b64 | xz -d > wip.patch && git apply --index wip.patch

# Exact numerics delivery: #470 and #443

## Contract and baseline

The primary issue removes the bounded public integer/decimal types, makes the
exact tower the only numeric value/API path, changes default division to exact
when terminating and otherwise 18 fractional places rounded half to even, and
makes temporal seconds exact. This reaches Rust, SPARQL, CLI, Python, C, and
sync/async WASM; the governor profile and vectors, CHANGELOG Breaking section,
English book, and zh-Hans translation must agree. Explicit `exact`, `N`, and
`N:ROUNDING` policies remain available.

The companion issue requires the exact tower to match bounded small-value
instruction counts, and large values to use measured subquadratic
multiplication, division, and radix conversion. It also requires selective
end-to-end evaluator dispatch based on measured wins, SIMD paths with portable
references and assembly registrations, fewer medium-value allocations, cheaper
rational GCD/reduction, sound governor costs, deterministic native/WASM answers,
and before/after SPARQL arithmetic, ORDER BY, SUM/AVG, and FILTER tables.

`.goals` calls for first-party Rust, maximal performance and wasm portability;
`.baseline` requires no silent incomplete work. The issue allows no new external
dependency without approval. The user removed exclusive timing campaigns from
the delivery list. Instruction-count work may use the available nonexclusive
machine; elapsed-time wins are not asserted from contended measurements.

This new #470 worktree is the sole implementation checkout. The old
`paudley/423-v4-decimal-defaults` commit is unreviewed donor code, not a passing
delivery; transfer useful units only after comparing against current main. The
#422 donor concerns a closed issue and may provide cases but is not copied
wholesale. Delete obsolete donor checkouts after verified transfer. Do not edit
S1's core/lex/Datalog/dictionary homes; coordinate shared evaluator/host files
and generated projections before editing them. `main` stays protected.

## Prior art and design boundary

Current main already has an inline exact `Integer`, three inline `BigInt`
limbs, bounded scratch, Karatsuba, exact costs, and the existing SIMD manifest.
It still defaults to truncating 18-place division, retains bounded numeric APIs
and temporal seconds, and uses the hybrid bounded evaluator path. The donor
implements much of the #470 core but explicitly leaves SPARQL assertions,
bindings, docs, and performance comparisons unfinished; its source predates the
geo and evaluator merges. Reconcile both sides at each production home.

No foundation-only precursor or default-only closure is acceptable. #443 may
ship independently only if its entire contract qualifies first; otherwise this
checkout delivers both complete issues. Do not turn missing measurements or
portability into a follow-up without an explicit user decision.

## Task 1: Reconcile exact-only XSD value and division law

Transfer the donor's useful XSD value and division logic into current main,
preserving newer geo/evaluator ownership and costs. Its temporal change is
insufficient: `temporal/seconds.rs` retains a private `Fixed { i128, u8 }` and
18-place ceiling behind exact public accessors. Replace the retained bounded
seconds storage and arithmetic with exact representation and tests on actual
sub-nanosecond and greater-than-18-place values. Remove bounded public
variants and conversions only when every production consumer is updated. Add
tests for terminating/nonterminating signs, ties, large coefficients/scales,
explicit policies, exact temporal arithmetic and canonical lexical identity.
Compile the XSD leaf and its immediately affected callers after coherent API
slices. Governed small and large operations must complete under adequate
declared work/scratch, and one-below work or storage admission must refuse
before output/owner mutation. Review the actual diff, commit normally with
hooks, and push.

## Task 2: Complete all numeric hosts and documentation

Propagate the exact-only API and division default through SPARQL evaluator,
CLI, Python, C, and sync/async WASM. Exercise installed/package entry points,
not only internal helpers. Bump and regenerate the governor profile/vectors
without rewriting older profiles. Update CHANGELOG Breaking, English book and
zh-Hans together with actual API signatures. Qualify explicit policy opt-ins,
error mapping, temporal seconds and deterministic native/WASM results. The
cross-host table includes a terminating quotient longer than 18 places,
`2 / 3`, an explicit half-even tie, and a long fractional temporal second,
with equal lexical values and typed errors. Review, commit with hooks and push.

## Task 3: Small-value parity and evaluator dispatch

Preserve the original seven-row bounded baseline inputs and executable before
bounded API removal. Compare old bounded and exact tower under the same
explicit `18:toward-zero` division law, same fixed work and recorded toolchain;
measure the new exact-first default separately. Bring each
decimal row to bounded parity or better, including multiply/divide and
parse/render/float conversion. Measure complete SPARQL arithmetic, ORDER BY,
SUM/AVG and FILTER lanes and select exact tower operations only where the
complete query does not regress. Keep exactness, multiplicity, errors and
governor accounting unchanged. Record instruction counts and allocation
quantities; do not require exclusive wall timing. Review, commit and push.

## Task 4: Large arithmetic and radix algorithms

Implement and tune Toom above Karatsuba, a larger-size transform path, a
subquadratic divide, and divide-and-conquer decimal parse/render with cached
powers. Prove product/quotient/remainder and lexical parity across threshold
boundaries against independent exact oracles. Record instruction-count sweeps
on native and portable WASM, work curves from 40 to 40,000 digits, and
thresholds. Cost bounds must cover every recursive scratch/result and never
under-report. Review, commit and push.

## Task 5: SIMD, allocation, rational reduction

Inspect compiled limb loops on x86_64-v3/v4, aarch64 NEON and wasm simd128;
add a path only where it actually vectorizes or a deliberate vector kernel wins.
Every added path has a portable reference, frozen goldens and manifest site.
Reduce medium-value allocations using existing inline/scratch ownership,
qualify with the shared allocator probes, and improve GCD/reduction for chained
rational operations without changing canonical results. Recheck exact cost
bounds and simultaneous peak storage. Review, commit and push.

## Task 6: Complete qualification and integration

Run the exact oracle properties, native/WASM deterministic digests, relevant
assembly configurations, cross-architecture runtime checks, installed host
tests and the required full repository gate on settled source. Keep benchmark
rows and `docs/BENCHMARKS.md`/`docs/design/purrdf-simd.md` synchronized with
actual measurements. The one broad gate is scheduled after focused repairs;
rerun affected coverage when source changes. Obtain independent material review
of final behavior, reconcile current main without discarding either side, and
record candid remaining failures. Stage artifacts document commands, outputs,
source applicability and risk; a passing narrow suite is not broad acceptance.

## Task 7: Publish and merge

After both entire contracts pass, create a PR that closes #443 and #470,
resolve review findings, satisfy hosted checks, post final notes and merge only
through `/home/paudley/stage/root/bin/ghprsq` with selected Stage evidence.
Verify both issue closures and the ordinary mirror, then remove this delivery
branch/worktree and obsolete donor products. No hook bypass, unreviewed donor
bulk merge, silent scope cut, or exclusive timing campaign is part of the work.

Exact-only numeric and temporal source is now committed and pushed as `fff66a72e`. The unqualified #443 Toom/parser experiments were removed from this branch and retained under the existing Stage task evidence for their separate full contract.

On the current source, strict XSD Clippy and the complete XSD crate suite passed (412 library tests, 30 exact-governance tests, 53 doctests and the other targets). The ordinary frozen governor profile v18 replay passed 15 tests with its regeneration test intentionally ignored. Final-source CLI exact numeric tests passed 8/8, and the 154 generated documentation claims agree. The normal commit hook, including the staged non-Rust ratchet, and the push passed.

This is a partial checkpoint. The C/Python/WASM packages need rebuilding and their current-source host suites, cross-host lexical/error comparison, portable release checks, generated conformance document, complete repository gates and final independent review remain. No PR or issue closure is claimed yet.

The obsolete bounded decimal comparison exemption is removed in 50ae94847, committed through normal hooks and pushed to the existing delivery branch. It named a comparison that now exists only under cfg(test), while production ordering uses exact::Decimal; the checker correctly rejected the stale registration.

Only that eight-line exemption was removed. The enforced bigint detector, all other live variants and checker remain intact. The existing helper gate passes 81 enforced jobs,21 live variants,118 distinct groups and 128 hash domains. Independent scoped review and the user's clarification that there is no tooling freeze are recorded in the delivery Stage.

This resolves the demonstrated registration failure. Exact/default host acceptance and final full qualification remain open, so no issue completion is claimed.

# Exact defaults on current main

The exact-default branch now includes the qualified host/evaluator fixes and the
complete capacity/storage delivery. Both integrations were committed with normal
hooks and published. Production source merged without conflict. The documentation
resolution retains the numeric, projection and graph-default guidance; standard
gettext regeneration and checks pass without modifying tools.

Current Rust, CLI, Python, C and WASM all-target compilation passes. The focused
operation regression confirms that division policy reaches every operation kind.
The complete optimized package is building from the current integrated source.
Earlier numeric, temporal, governor and portable receipts retain their recorded
scope; the old failed depth-floor package is not a pass.

Remaining acceptance is the current installed numeric/temporal host execution,
complete optimized package, final required repository gate, material review and
hosted checks. The public Rust numeric API change is intended for the documented
4.0 migration; this publication is not a registry release. The separate numeric
kernel optimization contract remains open.
